speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Health in light of the US research paper suggesting that COVID-19 reinfection is more dangerous (a) what is the mortality rate and serious complication rate of those in Singapore catching COVID-19 for a second or third time vis-a-vis a first-time infection; and (b) how does vaccination alter the mortality and severe illness rate in both groups.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I am afraid the media reports have not been clear or accurate.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The paper cited by the Member does not compare the severity between first-time infections and reinfections.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Instead, it compares the outcomes of those who had a first COVID-19 infection, versus those with two or more infections.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And therefore, not surprisingly, the study found it is more likely for persons to develop adverse health outcomes after two or more episodes of COVID-19 infection, compared to people who had only one infection episode.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Put it simply: getting sick twice is worse than getting sick once; but getting sick for the second time is not worse than getting sick the first time.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Is there any data that the bivalent vaccine booster has helped to reduce severe illness and death?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What is the uptake of the bivalent vaccine?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And with the Singapore public treating living with COVID as a new normal, how can we improve the uptake of the bivalent vaccine?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I do not have the breakdown, but the take-up has been encouraging for people keeping their vaccination up-to-date.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I just want to ask the Minister is there data to show what is the reinfection rate and the seriousness of using mRNA and other vaccines.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: My question is, is there data to show what is the effective rates of using mRNA and the seriousness of reinfection, and the difference between mRNA vaccine and others, these two categories.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There was a similar Parliamentary Question before and I showed some of the data.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Member should be able to find it in the Hansard.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Essentially, for the non-mRNA vaccine, we mostly use Sinovac.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Sinovac is effective if you take three or more shots, preferably four shots.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, both are effective, with mRNA vaccines having an edge over Sinovac.
